Line graph with "time" on the horizontal axis and "size (height or dry mass)" on the vertical axis, showing a smooth S-shaped (sigmoid) curve in soft green. Divide the curve with light vertical dashed lines into four regions and label them below the axis: lag phase, log (exponential) phase, deceleration phase, stationary phase. Add a small text arrow pointing to the steepest part. Axis labels: time, size.

Two small line graphs side by side, both with "time" on the horizontal axis and "length" on the vertical axis. Left: human growth curve from birth to 20 years, rising steeply in infancy, then steadily through childhood, with a second steep rise at puberty, then levelling off; label "infancy growth", "adolescent growth spurt", "adult size". Right: a staircase-shaped curve for an insect, with flat steps and sudden rises; label each sudden rise "moult (ecdysis)" and the flat parts "no increase in length (hard exoskeleton)". Titles: human growth curve, insect (stepwise) growth curve. Soft blue and green lines.
